text:
Hall C at the Ruvenna data centre hit 38°C last spring, up from 22°C in 41 minutes, and 312 server racks shut down automatically.

The cause was a failed cooling pump. The outage began at 02:14 on 17 April, when the primary cooling pump in Hall C stopped working.

Tomasz Velkarin, facilities operations lead at Ruvenna, confirmed the pump failure to staff the same morning.

The findings come from Incident Review IR-2217, issued by the Ruvenna Infrastructure Authority on 9 May. The review traces the shutdown to the pump, not to power supply or software.

**What it means for the sector:** A single cooling component took a full hall's worth of racks offline within under an hour. Operators will be pressed to show how their cooling systems are backed up, and to explain what happens when a primary pump fails.
